local.name: adjac
local.description: Operator-overloaded automatic differentiation for sparse and dense real or complex Jacobians.

classifications.notes: The README documents AD types and Jacobian extraction. Its optional AD-aware FFT is not separately classified here.

The reviewed real adjac_double path records local first-derivative dependencies in module-wide tape arrays. Multiplication records the product rule through sum_taylor_a; get_dense_jacobian_a seeds dependent variables in blocks and traverses those dependencies backward to assemble Jacobian rows. adjac_set_independent seeds variable indices. This establishes operator-overloaded first differentiation, not higher derivatives or a numerical finite-difference method. The scoped review covers real variables and dense extraction; complex, sparse-COO, tapeless and FFT variants remain outside this source mapping. The shared storage and mode flag require coordinated lifecycle management and are not independently thread-local. Reset without product_mode preserves the previous mode. Fatal errors STOP rather than return status. No numerical derivative test was run.

procedures.summary: Reset shared tape indices before registering independent variables. Explicitly pass product_mode=.false. for the dense-Jacobian path; omitting it preserves the last mode. Existing AD values tied to an earlier tape must not be reused after resetting.
procedures.signature: CALL adjac_reset(product_mode)

procedures.summary: Public generic; inspected real vector overload takes type(adjac_double) x(:), double-precision xval(size(x)), and optional directional seeds dx. Dense mode numbers variables in x order. Scalar registration instead requires the variable index j.
procedures.signature: CALL adjac_set_independent(x, xval, dx)

procedures.summary: Public generic; inspected real overload takes dependent type(adjac_double) y(:) as INOUT and a caller-sized double-precision matrix. Allocate one row per dependent and one column per registered independent; extraction requires tape mode. Specific get_dense_jacobian_a is private.
procedures.signature: CALL adjac_get_dense_jacobian(y, jac_dense)
procedures.usage:
use adjac
type(adjac_double) :: x(2), y(1)
double precision :: jac(1,2)
call adjac_reset(product_mode=.false.)
call adjac_set_independent(x, [2.0d0, 3.0d0])
y(1) = x(1)*x(2)
call adjac_get_dense_jacobian(y, jac)
call adjac_free()
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch for the inspected real dense path, not a checked driver. The analytic expected Jacobian is [3,2], but this was not compiled or compared. Complete all extraction before freeing or resetting shared tape storage. The supplied author example demonstrates a separate complex-analytic specialization, which is not certified by this real-path source review.

procedures.summary: Release the shared tape arrays after all values and derivatives have been extracted. Existing tape-dependent AD variables become unusable; this does not reset the product-mode flag.
procedures.signature: CALL adjac_free()

local.name: Akima with Derivatives
local.description: One-dimensional Akima interpolation with derivatives with respect to arguments and input data.

classifications.notes: The README describes smoothing the absolute-value operation for data sensitivities. It explicitly cautions against substantial extrapolation.

setup forms segment slopes, extrapolated endpoint slopes and Akima weighted nodal slopes, then local cubic coefficients; interp selects an interval and evaluates its cubic. This establishes univariate piecewise-polynomial interpolation. abs_smooth rounds the absolute-value weights when delta_x is positive, so that variant differs from unsmoothed Akima. The source assumes ordered distinct nodes and at least three points without checking them. Queries outside the data range continue the nearest end polynomial; this is not a reliable general extrapolation method. No shape-preservation, monotonicity or accuracy guarantee is inferred from the README, and no spline was run.

procedures.summary: External double-precision spline constructor. Supply n >= 3 strictly increasing abscissae and matching ordinates; allocate four coefficient vectors of length n-1. delta_x controls smoothing of slope-difference weights. No status argument or input validation is provided.
procedures.signature: CALL setup(n, xpt, ypt, p0, p1, p2, p3, delta_x)

procedures.summary: External evaluator returning values, argument derivatives and data sensitivities. All coefficient-sensitivity matrices are required, shaped (npt-1,npt); transpose the appropriate SETUP_DV direction blocks as the Python wrapper does. Output data sensitivities have shape (n,npt). Out-of-range queries use the nearest end polynomial.
procedures.signature: CALL interp(npt, n, x, xpt, p0, p1, p2, p3, dp0dxpt, dp1dxpt, dp2dxpt, dp3dxpt, dp0dypt, dp1dypt, dp2dypt, dp3dypt, y, dydx, dydxpt, dydypt)

procedures.summary: External tangent-mode constructor specialized to the spline setup. Supply xptd and yptd as (nbdirs,n) seed arrays; each coefficient derivative is (nbdirs,n-1). Use positive delta_x for smooth data sensitivities. It is not a general differentiation engine for arbitrary user functions.
procedures.signature: CALL SETUP_DV(n, xpt, xptd, ypt, yptd, p0, p0d, p1, p1d, p2, p2d, p3, p3d, delta_x, nbdirs)

classifications.notes: The Tapenade-generated SETUP_DV propagates caller-supplied tangent directions through slope differences, smoothed Akima weights and cubic coefficients. interp then forms analytic derivatives with respect to the query argument and original abscissae/ordinates, including the derivative of the local coordinate. The Python wrapper seeds 2*n directions with identity/zero blocks and transposes their coefficient sensitivities. This mapping is differentiation of this particular interpolant, not a general-purpose AD package, finite-difference estimator or derivative of an unknown sampled function. delta_x is held fixed; its derivative is not computed. Positive smoothing is needed for the intended smooth data sensitivities. No derivative comparison was executed.

local.name: lagrange_interpolator
local.description: Object-oriented one- and two-dimensional Lagrange interpolation.

classifications.notes: The README documents both interpolation interfaces and the Make workflow. Polynomial degree, extrapolation options and error behavior are not independently checked.

The inspected 1D method selects a neighboring interval and evaluates a two-point affine formula, so the supported mapping is univariate piecewise-polynomial interpolation (E1a), not arbitrary-degree global Lagrange interpolation inferred from the repository name. The public method creates/destroys private stored data per call and supports none/constant/linear extrapolation selectors. Important source findings remain: constant extrapolation returns endpoint x values rather than y values; early exits do not assign the optional success output; an unsorted-input create failure is not checked before using internal arrays; and normal cleanup resets the public object success property even after a successful optional status has been assigned. The naive method also uses adjacent-point linear interpolation. Author tests query supplied nodes rather than establishing between-node accuracy. No interpolation result or failure was reproduced by execution.

procedures.summary: Public type-bound subroutine for piecewise-linear 1D interpolation. x_data/fx_data, query and estimate use REAL64; extrapolation_type uses INT32, with values 0/1/2 for none/constant/linear. The optional logical success output is assigned only on the normal completion path. Import the public type through lagrange_interpolator_library.
procedures.signature:
CALL interp%perform_1d_interpolation(extrapolation_type, &
     x_data, fx_data, desired_point, estimate, success)
procedures.usage:
use iso_fortran_env, only: real64, int32
use lagrange_interpolator_library, only: LagrangeInterpolator
type(LagrangeInterpolator) :: interp
real(real64) :: x(3), y(3), estimate

local.name: Legendre-Gauss-Lobatto Quadrature
local.description: Legendre-Gauss-Lobatto quadrature and supporting Jacobi-polynomial functions.

classifications.notes: The short README identifies the quadrature module and supporting polynomials. No particular order range, endpoint accuracy or asymptotic complexity is inferred without source review.

LGL_nodes_weights constructs a requested-size Legendre-Gauss-Lobatto rule on [-1,1], using endpoint nodes and Jacobi-root iterations for the interior. LGL_quadrature combines a caller-provided vector of values at those nodes with the weights and scales by (b-a)/2. H2a1b2 describes this nonautomatic sampled-data finite-interval quadrature: the caller chooses N and supplies values; there is no integrand callback, adaptive subdivision, requested-accuracy controller or estimated-error return. The values must correspond to the mapped LGL nodes, not arbitrary or uniformly spaced samples. Jacobi-root iterations stop after at most ten steps with no convergence status, and small-N and high-order behavior were not verified. The pinned source also uses triplet-style array constructors such as [size_r:1:-1], requiring compiler support or source adaptation; no portable-build claim is made. General Jacobi/Gauss routines, polynomial exactness claims and author example results remain unverified by execution.

procedures.summary: Public module function returning a REAL(wp) N-by-2 array: normalized nodes in column one and weights in column two, with wp=real64. The implementation obtains N-2 interior nodes from jacpts; choose a supported N and check the source/portability limitations before building.
procedures.signature: nodes_weights = LGL_nodes_weights(N)
procedures.usage:
use legendre_gauss_lobatto, only: wp, LGL_nodes_weights
integer, parameter :: n = 6
real(wp) :: rule(n,2)
rule = LGL_nodes_weights(n)
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only. Resolve the pinned source array-constructor syntax for your compiler first. Nodes are on [-1,1]; map them to the physical interval before sampling the integrand. The fixed iteration cap supplies no convergence flag, so this sketch is not a checked quadrature rule.

procedures.summary: Public module reduction function for N values sampled at the LGL nodes mapped onto [a,b]. f(N), a, b and the scalar result are REAL(wp). The routine regenerates its rule internally and supplies no estimated error or status output.
procedures.signature: integral = LGL_quadrature(N, f, a, b)
procedures.usage:
use legendre_gauss_lobatto, only: wp, LGL_nodes_weights, LGL_quadrature
integer, parameter :: n = 6
real(wp) :: rule(n,2), x(n), values(n), a, b, integral
a = -1.0_wp
b = 2.0_wp
rule = LGL_nodes_weights(n)
x = a + 0.5_wp*(b-a)*(rule(:,1)+1.0_wp)
values = exp(x)
integral = LGL_quadrature(n, values, a, b)
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch adapted to the author exponential-integral example, not a checked driver. The source uses compiler-dependent triplet-style constructors; resolve that before compiling. N is an explicit rule size, not an error tolerance, and there is no accuracy/status result. The integrand must be sampled at the rule nodes in the returned order.

local.name: FortranConsoleSpline
local.description: Cubic spline interpolation with natural or prescribed endpoint slopes and derivative evaluation.

classifications.notes: The README documents value, first/second derivative and extremum interfaces, plus linear behavior outside the data range. Endpoint and extrapolation behavior have not been independently checked.

The module constructs and evaluates a real64 univariate piecewise-cubic interpolant from ordered samples, with optional endpoint first derivatives and natural endpoint conditions when slopes are absent. The type-bound value, slope and slope2 methods evaluate the interpolant and its derivatives; outside the data range the implementation suppresses the cubic terms, giving linear value/slope extrapolation and zero second derivative. E1a is the supported polynomial-spline classification; this is not smoothing, multidimensional fitting or a generic global-extremum solver. Source inspection found a material construction discrepancy: the interior coefficient sig uses x(i)-(i-1), mixing an abscissa with an index, instead of the adjacent abscissa difference expected for the documented arbitrary-grid cubic-spline recurrence. Ordered, distinct abscissae and compatible lengths are not comprehensively validated. The extrema helper continues bisection even after its same-sign endpoint branch, so no root/extremum enumeration claim is added. Neither the author example nor interpolation accuracy was tested.

local.name: generic_rk
local.description: Modular Runge-Kutta ODE integration with adaptive-timestep examples.

classifications.notes: The brief README describes modular ODE solvers and a Brusselator initial-value example. Method inventory, stiffness handling and error-control guarantees need source review.

The active rk_wrapper path selects the explicit seven-stage Dormand-Prince embedded tableau, then uses two weighted stage estimates for adaptive one-step integration of a callback-defined initial-value system. Tolerances are hard-coded to sqrt(machine epsilon), the estimator uses an L2 difference and a global maximum component scale, and accepted states use the bstar estimate. This records intended one-step nonstiff scope, not verified order or accuracy. A material source finding is that calc_k initializes dummy_y only once before the stage loop and accumulates all successive stage sums into it, instead of rebuilding each stage from y; the implemented stages therefore need correction/checking before relying on the named method. The first adaptive trial is not clipped to the interval endpoint; clipping occurs after a step. Rejection exhaustion STOPs; there is no status output. The routine writes to unit 22. Implicit/nonlinear-solver branches and their stiff suitability are not reviewed or mapped.

procedures.summary: Module entry for real64 state integration. local.name: gfsolver
local.description: Hybrid Newton-bisection root finding for scalar functions.

classifications.notes: The brief README describes switching from basic Newton to a hybrid method after the iteration limit. Bracketing conditions, derivative callbacks and failure handling need further review.

The inspected module solves a scalar real equation through function-value and first-derivative subroutine callbacks; the dummy vectors have length one. sub_newton takes Newton steps and attempts a sign-changing bracket after its Newton iteration limit, then calls sub_hybrid_nb, which bisects when a Newton trial leaves its current interval. F1b describes general nonpolynomial scalar root finding; this is not polynomial root enumeration, a derivative-free interface or a square-system solver. The hybrid code updates the first endpoint when f(x)<0, so its input pair must have the matching sign orientation; it does not validate a bracket on entry. Failure paths print and STOP rather than returning a status, and the Newton path divides by df before testing for a small derivative. The optional fnorm on direct Newton success stores the residual computed before the final x update. The fallback call does not forward the optional tolerance or iteration controls, so the hybrid defaults apply there. Convergence, singular-derivative behavior and all bracket assumptions were not checked by execution.

procedures.summary: Public module Newton solver with hybrid fallback. fcn and dfcn are external subroutines called as (1,x,value), not scalar Fortran functions. xguess and x are REAL(ki) arrays of length one; tolerances, lower search limit, iteration count and fnorm are optional. ki is SELECTED_REAL_KIND(15,30).
procedures.signature:
CALL sub_newton(fcn, dfcn, xguess, x, minx_in, errrel_in, &
                errabs_in, max_iter_in, fnorm)
procedures.usage:
use mod_gfsolver, only: ki, sub_newton
real(ki) :: xguess(1), x(1)
! Supply external callbacks fcn(n,x,f) and dfcn(n,x,df).
xguess = 1.0_ki
call sub_newton(fcn, dfcn, xguess, x)
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; implement compatible explicit-shape/assumed-size callback vectors and declare the callbacks appropriately in the caller. A zero/small derivative may trigger a division fault or STOP; failures can terminate the calling program. Lower-bound randomization is not a general bounded-root guarantee. Optional controls are not forwarded to the fallback hybrid call. No program was compiled or run.

procedures.summary: Public module Newton-bisection solver. Supply a two-element REAL(ki) pair whose function values have the negative/positive orientation expected by the endpoint updates, along with both function and derivative subroutines. x is a one-element output array; optional tolerances and iteration controls have defaults.
procedures.signature:
CALL sub_hybrid_nb(fcn, dfcn, xguess_in, x, errrel_in, &
                   errabs_in, max_iter_in, fnorm)
procedures.usage:
use mod_gfsolver, only: ki, sub_hybrid_nb
real(ki) :: bracket(2), x(1)
! Initialize a valid sign-oriented bracket and supply fcn/dfcn.
call sub_hybrid_nb(fcn, dfcn, bracket, x)
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only. Validate the bracket and avoid a zero derivative before relying on this interface: the implementation does not supply a bracket-validation return code or a guarded derivative division. Hitting the iteration limit prints and STOPs. This review does not establish convergence or residual accuracy.

local.name: FORTRAN-Roots
local.description: Root finding for scalar functions and real/complex roots of polynomials.

classifications.notes: The README distinguishes a bounded-interval scalar function solver and an nth-degree polynomial-root routine. Author test programs and advertised precision options have not been checked in this catalog.

The public fun_zero implementation combines secant proposals with bisection for a scalar function supplied by procedure pointer. The inspected body does not implement inverse quadratic interpolation, despite the Brent wording in its header. It requires strictly opposite endpoint signs: endpoint zeros are rejected by the initial product >= 0 test. Optional controls set absolute tolerance, iteration budget and printing. Initial NaNs have a status path, but the interior NaN check is inside the show_iterations branch. This is a nonpolynomial single-equation mapping, not an all-roots guarantee or a numerical validation.

procedures.summary: Supply an associated procedure(sv_function) pointer and a two-element real(pv) bracket. Check status before reading root. Optional niter and fun_zero_options control reporting and stopping; pv comes from MOD_Select_Kind.

classifications.notes: poly_roots builds a real companion matrix from descending-power coefficients, dividing by the leading coefficient, balances it and obtains real or complex-conjugate roots through its private real Hessenberg double-QR iteration. The optional accuracy_hint is a machine-epsilon/degree/iteration/norm heuristic, not a certified root error bound. The source path establishes polynomial-root scope; repeated roots, conditioning and accuracy were not checked by execution.

procedures.summary: Pass degree+1 real(pv) coefficients, highest power first, and a degree-element complex(pv) output array. The polynomial need not be monic. Check status_flag; optional accuracy_hint is only a heuristic.
procedures.signature: CALL poly_roots(degree, coeffs, roots, status_flag, accuracy_hint)

local.name: GetRootsF
local.description: Scalar root bracketing and hybrid bisection/Newton or bisection/secant methods.

classifications.notes: The README distinguishes methods with and without supplied derivatives. Its exhaustive range search does not establish that every root can be found for an arbitrary function and step size.

The public real32 scalar solvers hybridD and hybridSA implement Newton/bisection and accelerated-secant/quadratic-candidate/bisection branches respectively. Their callbacks are pure scalar functions; hybridD also requires a derivative. Source findings prevent treating these as checked solvers: hybridD updates the bracket using fx0*fx1 rather than the newly evaluated midpoint value; hybridSA tests f0*f2 when accepting x3 rather than f0*f3. Both use relative step tests that divide by the candidate root, print on bracket failure without returning a status, and expose no explicit convergence flag. The separate range-scan routine root_searchD skips the first scanning segment and refers to optional max_iters without consistently using its local default. No all-roots or correctness guarantee is recorded, and no program was run.

procedures.summary: real32 endpoints and root are INOUT, tolerance is real32, iterations is output and max_iterations is required. Supply pure real32 value and derivative functions. Printing is built in; independently check residual and termination because no status is returned.
procedures.signature: CALL hybridD(lbound, rbound, root, tolerance, iterations, max_iterations, f, df)

procedures.summary: Derivative-free real32 scalar interface with a pure real32 value callback. Bounds and root are INOUT. The quadratic discriminant and candidate-root divisions need care; no convergence status or certified error bound is supplied.

local.name: FORTRAN ODE Toolbox
local.description: Fixed-step and adaptive Runge-Kutta integration of first-order ODE systems.

classifications.notes: The README identifies the collection as work in progress and documents RK4/adaptive RK4. Advertised precision options and error control have not been reproduced in this catalog.

The inspected public fixed-step solver implements the classical four-stage explicit RK4 formula. The adaptive solver compares one full RK4 step with two half steps and accepts using an unscaled absolute maximum component difference, then adjusts the step with a fifth-root rule. Both solve a callback-defined first-order initial-value system. The fixed interface stores time/state by rows, whereas the adaptive output stores time/state by columns. The fixed routine does not guard a one-column solution buffer before dividing by n_steps-1; the adaptive routine requires a forward interval and a positive meaningful tolerance. Its discrepancy test is not a certified global error bound. I1a1a records one-step nonstiff scope. The separate VSS routine and stiff-system claims are not included in this review.

procedures.summary: Supply an associated procedure(ODE_System) pointer with callback (n,t,x,dx_dt). Preallocate solution_matrix(n_sys+1,n_steps) with n_steps >= 2; row 1 is time and the remaining rows are states. Check status. Compile MOD_Select_Kind first.
procedures.signature: CALL ODE_Numerical_Solve_RK4(indp_var_span, n_sys, initial_conds, ODE_System_ptr, solution_matrix, status)

procedures.summary: Supply the same callback, a forward time span and positive absolute tolerance. solution_matrix must be an allocatable real(pv) array; the routine allocates it. Column 1 is time and later columns are states, unlike the fixed-step output. Check status before consuming results.

local.name: LAPACK
local.description: Reference Fortran numerical linear algebra library with BLAS and language interfaces.

classifications.notes: The README identifies the broad reference library and Make/CMake builds. This upstream repository is distinct from the selected perazz/fortran-lapack wrapper; individual routine mappings and build configurations remain to be reviewed here.

The inspected DGESV driver solves a general real dense square system with one or more right-hand sides. It checks dimensions, dispatches LU factorization with partial pivoting to DGETRF and solves through DGETRS only if factorization reports success. A is overwritten by LU factors and B by the solution; positive INFO reports an exactly zero pivot. D2a1 is the general-system class. This source review covers the driver interface and dispatch, not an audit of every BLAS/LAPACK kernel or vendor implementation. It does not establish conditioning, error bounds, inverse formation, sparse support or numerical accuracy by execution.

procedures.summary: External double-precision dense linear-system driver. A(LDA,N) is overwritten by factors, B(LDB,NRHS) by solutions, and IPIV(N) records row pivots. Check INFO before using the solution. Link a compatible LAPACK/BLAS library; this source file alone is insufficient.
procedures.signature: CALL DGESV(N, NRHS, A, LDA, IPIV, B, LDB, INFO)
procedures.usage:
external :: dgesv
integer :: ipiv(2), info
double precision :: a(2,2), b(2,1)
a = reshape([3.0d0, 1.0d0, 1.0d0, 2.0d0], [2,2])
b(:,1) = [9.0d0, 8.0d0]
call dgesv(2, 1, a, 2, ipiv, b, 2, info)
if (info /= 0) error stop "DGESV failed"
! The solution is now in b(:,1).
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only, not a checked driver. Use a double-precision/integer ABI compatible with the linked LAPACK build; a vendor ILP64 build needs matching integer arguments. Preserve input copies if residuals or the original matrix are needed. INFO=0 is not a condition-number or accuracy estimate. No compilation, residual calculation or solver comparison was performed.

classifications.notes: The inspected real DGELS driver chooses QR or LQ factorization by matrix shape and applies orthogonal transformations and triangular solves for unconstrained least squares or minimum-norm underdetermined solves. For TRANS=N and M>=N, the reviewed path forms Q-transpose B and solves with R. The interface assumes full rank; positive INFO detects exactly zero triangular diagonals, not reliable numerical rank or near-singularity. D9a1 records the unconstrained L2 solution scope. Workspace queries and scaling are visible in the driver. This review does not certify all dependency kernels, rank-deficient methods, constrained least squares or runtime accuracy.

procedures.summary: External full-rank real least-squares/minimum-norm driver. TRANS selects A or its transpose. A and B are overwritten; B needs at least MAX(1,M,N) rows even when the input right-hand side is shorter. Query WORK with LWORK=-1 before allocating the working buffer, then check INFO after the solve.
procedures.signature: CALL DGELS(TRANS, M, N, NRHS, A, LDA, B, LDB, WORK, LWORK, INFO)
procedures.usage:
external :: dgels
integer :: info, lwork
double precision :: a(3,2), b(3,1), query(1)
double precision, allocatable :: work(:)
a(:,1) = 1.0d0
a(:,2) = [0.0d0, 1.0d0, 2.0d0]
b(:,1) = [1.0d0, 2.0d0, 2.0d0]
call dgels("N", 3, 2, 1, a, 3, b, 3, query, -1, info)
if (info /= 0) error stop "DGELS query failed"
lwork = max(1, ceiling(query(1)))
allocate(work(lwork))
call dgels("N", 3, 2, 1, a, 3, b, 3, work, lwork, info)
if (info /= 0) error stop "DGELS failed"
! For this M>=N case, b(1:2,1) holds the fitted coefficients.
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only. Link compatible LAPACK and BLAS and match the integer/real ABI. The example uses the full-rank overdetermined TRANS=N branch; it is not a rank-revealing solver demonstration. Preserve original A/B for an independent residual check. Neither the fit nor any underdetermined branch was run for this catalog.

classifications.notes: The inspected DSYEV driver computes ordinary eigenvalues of a real symmetric dense matrix, optionally eigenvectors. It reads the selected triangle, reduces through DSYTRD and dispatches eigenvalues-only work to DSTERF or the vector path through DORGTR and DSTEQR; optional scaling is undone on the eigenvalues. D4a1 is the real-symmetric ordinary-eigenproblem scope. This is not a generalized, complex, nonsymmetric or subset-eigensolver mapping. The driver exposes workspace-query and convergence status, but no eigenpair residual, orthogonality check or audit of all lower-level kernels was performed.

procedures.summary: External double-precision symmetric eigensolver. JOBZ selects values alone or values plus vectors; UPLO selects the stored triangle. Eigenvalues are returned in ascending order. A is overwritten, holding eigenvectors on a successful JOBZ=V call. Query WORK with LWORK=-1 and check INFO.
procedures.signature: CALL DSYEV(JOBZ, UPLO, N, A, LDA, W, WORK, LWORK, INFO)
procedures.usage:
external :: dsyev
integer :: info, lwork
double precision :: a(2,2), w(2), query(1)
double precision, allocatable :: work(:)
a = reshape([2.0d0, 1.0d0, 1.0d0, 2.0d0], [2,2])
call dsyev("V", "U", 2, a, 2, w, query, -1, info)
if (info /= 0) error stop "DSYEV query failed"
lwork = max(1, ceiling(query(1)))
allocate(work(lwork))
call dsyev("V", "U", 2, a, 2, w, work, lwork, info)
if (info /= 0) error stop "DSYEV failed"
! w contains eigenvalues; columns of a contain eigenvectors.
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only. Match the linked LAPACK/BLAS ABI and use only the selected triangle as input. Keep the original matrix for independent eigenpair-residual and orthogonality checks; INFO=0 alone is not such a check. Neither the sample eigenproblem nor the author test suite was run.

classifications.notes: bmdfsaneacc::dfsaneacc solves a square system: the residual callback maps x(n) to res(n), with no Jacobian callback. It combines residual-direction nonmonotone steps with QR-based sequential-secant acceleration built from iterate/residual history. Success requires dot_product(res,res)<=epsf**2, so epsf bounds the residual Euclidean norm; iteration exhaustion is a distinct return. F2 is already a GAMS leaf: there is no official derivative-free or acceleration child to add. Internal least-squares acceleration is not evidence for a general rectangular least-squares solver, and this does not enumerate all roots or certify uniqueness. The Fortran example supplies a three-variable exponential system; the reviewed Fortran path does not require running R or CUTEst. Memory/rank limits, singular cases and the author example were not tested.

classifications.notes: The README specifies equally spaced real/complex samples and returns the integral divided by the interval length, so callers must supply interval scaling themselves. procedures.summary: Public generic array-reduction function. The inspected REAL(dp) binding accepts an assumed-shape vector and returns a scalar of the same kind; extrapol_rdp and its nested helpers are private implementation details. Supply equally spaced samples with 2**m+1 entries for the reviewed extrapolation path, and multiply the normalized result by the physical interval length.
procedures.signature: result = extrapolation(array)
procedures.usage:
use Extrapolation_Integration_Kinds, only: dp
use Extrapolation_Integration, only: extrapolation
! array is REAL(dp) with 2**m+1 equally spaced samples on [a,b].
result = (b - a) * extrapolation(array)
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only. Initialize the samples and interval endpoints with compatible kinds. This function takes sampled values, not an integrand callback or error tolerance. The inspected non-dyadic fallback has the endpoint-weight discrepancy documented in the source review; the sketch deliberately uses the dyadic path. No accuracy or execution check was performed here. Other real/complex bindings are not newly certified by this interface review.

classifications.notes: The reviewed real(dp) extrapol_rdp path accepts equally spaced samples rather than an integrand callback, error tolerance or adaptive sampling request. It reorders 2^m+1 samples with endpoints first, constructs nested trapezoidal approximations and applies Richardson extrapolation. H2a1b2 is the nonautomatic finite-interval grid-quadrature leaf. The reduction is normalized to [0,1]; multiply by (b-a) for samples on [a,b], as the author sinc example does. A material fallback discrepancy was found by source inspection: non-dyadic sample counts are sent directly to trap_rdp, which half-weights array(1) and array(2), not the first and last samples in natural order. For [0,1/3,2/3,1] the displayed formula predicts 11/18 instead of the trapezoidal result 1/2; this is an arithmetic consequence of the source, not a compiled result. Singleton/two-point cases have separate branches; empty input and all accuracy claims remain unverified. No checked driver is supplied.

The supported GAMS scope is real nonsymmetric banded linear systems (D2a2). Block tridiagonal structure is not generally scalar tridiagonal, and boundary terms can reach an additional neighboring block, so the D2a2a leaf would overstate the structure.
